name: Acres for America Program
summary: Large grants to land trusts and conservation organisations for permanently protecting habitat through land purchases and perpetual conservation easements across the United States. Two-stage annual round; the 2027 pre-proposal stage has closed.

eligibility.rule: Not a U.S. Federal government agency, business, unincorporated individual or international organization
Do not use NFWF funds for ongoing legal-compliance efforts
A fee transfer or perpetual conservation easement qualifies for conservation purposes under IRC Section 170(h)
Make all acquisition documents available for NFWF staff review
Grant pays only toward the purchase price of the property

calls.label: 2027 Request for Proposals
calls.note: Pre-proposals are closed; full proposals, due December 2, 2026, are by invitation only

status.quote: Pre-Proposal Due Date October 19, 2026, 11:59 PM ET

deadline.quote: Pre-Proposal Due Date October 19, 2026, 11:59 PM ET

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include non-profit 501(c) organizations, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal governments and organizations, and educational institutions.

geography.quote: Acres for America is a nationwide program.

access.quote: This Request for Proposals (RFP) will collect pre-proposals from around the nation

window.quote: This program runs annually as a two-phased application.

amount.quote: Individual grant awards are expected to range from $250,000 to $1 million, depending on project scope, conservation value, and readiness.

co_finance_required.quote: All grant awards require a minimum 1:1 match of cash or contributed goods and services.

eligibility.quote: Ineligible applicants include U.S. Federal government agencies, businesses, unincorporated individuals, and international organizations.
NFWF funds may not be used to support ongoing efforts to comply with legal requirements, including permit conditions, mitigation and settlement agreements.
The fee transfer or perpetual conservation easement must qualify for "conservation purposes" as defined by Internal Revenue Code Section 170(h), which generally includes the following:

All acquisition documents, including appraisals, title reports, environmental hazard assessments, mineral rights assessments, surveys, and where appropriate a local attorney's opinion of easement viability, as well as other appropriate documents, must be available for NFWF staff review as part of the application process.
Grant funds from the Acres for America program can only be applied to the property's purchase price.

documents.quote: Pre-Proposal Narrative: The most important upload is your actual pre-proposal narrative.
Project Site Map: Please provide a map(s) delineating the land proposed for conservation in the context of adjacent protected lands (e.g., federal, state, private lands, conservation easements).
